A1.justification: Both complete 45-page PDFs describe the same ICRL study. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support comparison of the main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Pages 16–45, including the appendices and checklist, are identical.

before.justification: v1 reports original ICRL molecular prediction experiments in Sections 3–5, with additional protein, drug-target interaction, molecular QA/captioning, vision, and audio results in Appendix F.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results in the main text and Appendix F, including numerical comparisons, ablations, and attention analyses.

M1.justification: The PCA, Zero-Pad, random projection, and OT-based injection procedures and Appendix D algorithms are unchanged. The small wording edit to the Zero-Pad paragraph describes the same normalization procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same molecular property, protein, drug-target interaction, molecular QA/captioning, and vision/audio datasets and tasks. Appendix F introduces no additional coverage relative to v1.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments, including ICL and injection controls, MolecularGPT/GIMLET/SELFormer/GPT-MolBERTa in Table 3, and the QA, captioning, and vision/audio comparisons in Appendix F.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 and Appendices F–G retain the same model configurations, sample sizes, metrics, demonstration sampling, PCA dimensions, shot counts, and batch-query settings. No evaluation protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The projector activation/initialization, PCA dimensionality, shot/query-size, and feature-layer ablations are unchanged. Attention, representation-similarity, and decoded-prompt analyses in Sections 4–5 and Appendices F–G are also retained.

E5.justification: The main experiments retain ten random seeds and top-three-run reporting. Supplementary repeated-run descriptions, reported uncertainty values, and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted trends, and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 2 retains ESOL Pearson correlations of 0.465 for ICL and 0.542 for OT-PCA+ICL.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, OT alignment equations, Theorems 1–2, Corollary 1, and their Appendix E proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the same training-free multimodal integration claim, proof-of-concept objective, three research questions, and contributions concerning design choices and mechanistic insights. The abstract and conclusion have unchanged scientific meaning.

C2.justification: Interpretations involving representation diversity, alignment, task-learning versus task-retrieval modes, and pause-token behavior are retained. Limitations concerning supervised-method performance and homogeneous protein representations also remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The acknowledgment newly states that part of the computational work used National Supercomputing Centre resources in Singapore. This is a limited computing-resource disclosure; implementation details, hyperparameters, and code/data-access statements are otherwise unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 6, Appendix B, and the bibliography retain the same cited works and research positioning, including the distinction from Vector-ICL and supervised multimodal approaches. Reference entries merely reflow across pages.

P1.justification: v3 expands and revises author affiliations, adds the NSCC acknowledgment, and lightly edits wording and punctuation in the Zero-Pad description. The section sequence and substantive narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded affiliation block and longer acknowledgment cause limited text, figure-position, spacing, and reference-page reflow. Figure and table designs, captions, and contents are retained, and the appendix layout is identical.

improvement.justification: v3 improves attribution through revised affiliations and the NSCC credit, but the methods, evidence, proofs, interpretations, and complete appendices remain unchanged. The limited wording and layout edits do not materially improve or diminish the paper's scientific support, clarity, or reproducibility.
